new_sources.title: Agent Behavioral Contracts II: Certifying Compositional Reliability Without Assuming Independence
Nine Judges, Two Effective Votes: Correlated Errors Undermine LLM Evaluation Panels
Diversity Collapse in Multi-Agent LLM Systems: Structural Coupling and Collective Failure in Open-Ended Idea Generation

candidate_mechanisms.description: Do not assume two reviewer/research agents supply independent evidence merely because they run separately or use different prompts. Measure joint failure directly with deterministic or externally grounded scoring. If a reliability claim must be composed, use dependence-aware moment bounds rather than multiplying marginal reliabilities under an untested independence assumption.
quantitative_evidence: Preregistered confirmatory experiment: 18,000 two-agent handoff missions, 6,000 per arm, with deterministic gold scoring and no LLM judge; larger campaign 30,820 scored missions across three topologies.

Same-model pair (mistral-small-24b × mistral-small-24b): agent failure rates 39.4% and 37.2%; independence predicts 14.6% co-failure but observed co-failure is 36.3%. Among 2,418 missions where either failed, both failed on 2,177 = 90.0%. log odds ratio 6.6645 [6.3827, 7.0015], phi 0.9161 [0.9057, 0.9261].

Substituting a different model significantly reduced marginal-free failure association in six of six same-model-vs-different-model contrasts across series, quorum, and parallel topologies; log-OR reductions were about 1.2–2.1 units depending on contrast/topology.
Changing vendor after model identity already differed did not yield a consistent further reduction; the registered three-level vendor ordering did not replicate.

An unmanipulated same-model negative-control pair present in all arms returned 15/15 null arm contrasts, supporting attribution of the manipulated pair changes to model substitution rather than graph-wide drift.

On four-component data, enriching the measured co-execution moment set from 10 to 14 functionals narrowed the identified reliability interval by 85.7% and raised the certified floor from 0.2455 to 0.4116 without assuming a dependence model.
candidate_mechanisms.evidence_scope: Retail and financial contract tasks with Mistral/Ministral/Gemma models. Model identity is confounded with capability because substituted models differ in competence; arms use independent draws rather than paired missions. The paper explicitly does not claim its dependence magnitudes transfer to code generation, research synthesis, or open-ended dialogue. The direction is therefore a candidate to test in O, not a measured property of O or these ChatGPT workers.
candidate_mechanisms.decision_relevance: Very high. O, chat-side research, and many verifier/reviewer roles can share a base model. Agreement or repeated success from same-model instances should not be counted as independent evidence without measured dependence. When independence matters, model substitution is a plausible intervention, but vendor diversity by itself is not supported by this experiment.

candidate_mechanisms.description: When using an LLM evaluator panel, estimate effective independent information from item-level error correlations against human or deterministic ground truth. Do not treat panel size, family count, unanimity, or more sophisticated aggregation as equivalent to independent evidence.
quantitative_evidence: Nine frontier judges from seven model families on 1,000 ChaosNLI-MNLI items yielded effective sample size n_eff=2.18 [2.07,2.31], eigenvalue estimate 2.16, mean pairwise phi 0.391, and independence ratio 24.2%.
MNLI panel accuracy was 72.0% versus best individual 71.8%, while an independence-calibrated Condorcet model predicted about 94%, a 22.0 percentage-point gap [19.5,24.1].
Replication: SNLI n_eff=2.35 and panel 77.7% versus best individual 84.2%; AlphaNLI n_eff=2.48 and panel 88.7% versus best individual 91.2%; RewardBench n_eff=1.99.
Adding judges 6-9 added only +0.22 effective votes; 9-judge effective independence asymptoted around 2.6 under the measured correlation.

Same-family correlations were only slightly above cross-family mean on MNLI (about +0.047). The three most correlated judge pairs were cross-family, and restricting to one judge per family reduced n_eff to 1.93. Family labels alone therefore did not recover independence.
Dawid-Skene and oracle-informed weighting closed at most 11% of the Condorcet gap across stable methods; on three of four datasets the best individual judge beat all aggregation methods.
candidate_mechanisms.evidence_scope: NLI and RewardBench evaluation tasks, nine specific 2026 judges, majority-human or deterministic labels. This is not a scientist-agent experiment and does not establish the same effective sample size for O's evaluators. It does show that even cross-family diversity can retain high shared error correlation, so cross-model review must be calibrated rather than assumed independent.
candidate_mechanisms.decision_relevance: Very high for O evaluation design: evaluator quorum should be weighted by measured error dependence/calibration, not nominal judge count. Cross-model review is a candidate independence intervention, but evidence from this study warns that family diversity alone may still leave strong correlation.

candidate_mechanisms.description: For open-ended scientific ideation, generate independent trajectories before exposing agents to each other's conclusions; use sparse/subgroup or nominal-group interaction rather than dense authority-driven deliberation when diversity is the objective. Model heterogeneity can increase semantic exploration, but its benefit depends on interaction structure.
quantitative_evidence: Study evaluates more than 10,000 research proposals across 20 topics. Human validation of diversity metrics found 87% agreement for Vendi Score, 82% for structural disorder, and 81% for pairwise cosine dispersion.
Horizontal junior-dominated collaboration had Vendi 8.08 versus interdisciplinary authority-weighted Vendi 4.65, while overall quality differed much less (7.88 versus 8.50).
Increasing group size from 3 to 7 increased absolute diversity but Diversity Utilization Ratio fell from 1.03 to 0.47, showing strong diminishing information gain per added agent.

Heterogeneous DSV3+GPT-4o+Claude under authority-weighted conditions increased Vendi by +34.0% for Interdisciplinary (p=0.0003, d=2.33) and +14.6% for Leader-Led (p=0.071, d=0.99), but gave no gain in the small 5-topic Horizontal comparison (-4.1%, p=0.627).

Across the full 20-topic horizontal comparison, mixed-model Horizontal reached Vendi 3.402±0.332 versus DeepSeek-V3 Horizontal with delta +0.648, paired p=0.000046, with 19/20 topics showing higher diversity; it also exceeded GPT-5.1 Horizontal by +0.534 (p<0.0001).
candidate_mechanisms.evidence_scope: Scientific proposal ideation diversity, not downstream experiment success. Heterogeneous authority comparison used only five topics and fixed model assignment; full 20-topic heterogeneous result is a diversity result, not evidence of higher scientific correctness or AGI progress.
candidate_mechanisms.decision_relevance: High for the external-research-worker architecture: many same-model workers should remain topic/context-isolated during discovery rather than densely sharing intermediate hypotheses. Raw worker count has diminishing diversity returns. Integrate after independent exploration, and evaluate heterogeneity only if it yields downstream decision improvements rather than diversity for its own sake.

new_failure_evidence.observation: Independent invocations can share failure modes strongly enough that nominal redundancy overstates actual evidence. In the preregistered contract experiment, same-model co-failure occurred on 90% of missions where either failed; in a separate nine-judge panel, nine votes contained only about 2.2 effective independent votes on MNLI.
new_failure_evidence.scope: Different tasks and metrics; do not numerically combine the two studies or transfer their magnitudes to O without matched testing.
new_failure_evidence.implication: O/chat/reviewer agreement should not be promoted to independent confirmation solely because it came from separate calls or personas.

new_failure_evidence.observation: Cross-family judge pairs can be more correlated than same-family pairs; restricting to one judge per family did not increase effective independence in the tested panel.
new_failure_evidence.implication: If O adds a second model for verification, measure complementarity on matched errors rather than assuming vendor/family diversity is sufficient.

new_failure_evidence.observation: Increasing agents expanded absolute idea diversity but sharply reduced diversity gained per agent; authority/dense interaction accelerated convergence, while independent-first or subgroup processes preserved more exploration.
new_failure_evidence.scope: Research-proposal ideation; no downstream execution endpoint.
new_failure_evidence.implication: Do not maximize research-worker count without measuring marginal novel evidence. Keep workers independent and prune/retarget redundant trajectories based on unique evidence yield.

architecture_implications_for_current_ex: Keep discovery workers isolated by topic and durable state; do not broadcast one worker's hypothesis to all others before they independently search.
The integrator should deduplicate and rank evidence, not use worker consensus count as confidence unless worker error dependence has been calibrated.

If multiple workers independently converge on the same source/result, preserve provenance but treat convergence as corroboration only to the extent their retrieval/evaluation paths are genuinely independent.

If a non-Work different-model resource becomes available, test its marginal complementarity on held-out scientist-agent evidence judgments before allocating routine budget; model/vendor label is an insufficient proxy for independence.
Track marginal unique-source/mechanism yield per worker/time. Adding workers should stop or retarget when novel evidence yield saturates, even if absolute worker count can be increased.
dead_ends_or_cautions: Do not claim the 90% same-model co-failure magnitude applies to ChatGPT/O; the primary paper explicitly limits task-domain transfer and model identity is partly confounded with capability.

Do not infer cross-vendor diversity is useless. One preregistered experiment only found no further vendor effect after model identity changed, while a separate judge-panel study found family labels insufficient for independence. The proper conclusion is to measure error complementarity directly.
Do not optimize the research workers for semantic diversity alone. The Diversity Collapse paper measures ideation diversity, not correctness or downstream scientific success.
Do not count nine-judge unanimity as near-certainty; the primary panel had 9.1% error even on unanimous MNLI items.
next_queries: Find scientist-agent or research-evaluator experiments that directly compare same-model versus cross-model reviewer correctness against external scientific ground truth, not only contract or NLI tasks.
Find controlled methods to select complementary evaluators using observed error covariance or effective independence rather than provider/model labels.
Find downstream experiments connecting independent-first ideation or heterogeneous proposal generation to implemented research quality, not only diversity metrics.
Find dynamic worker-allocation methods that maximize marginal novel evidence per compute while preserving independent exploration.
Continue transfer/applicability calibration and external-oracle searches from records 006-007.

continuation.exact_resume_from: Continue after record 008. Priority: matched same-vs-cross-model scientific reviewer experiments, covariance-based evaluator selection, downstream value of independent-first ideation, dynamic worker allocation by marginal novel evidence, and validated memory applicability. Do not re-cover records 001-008 unless extracting new causal evidence, primary verification, replication, or contradiction.
